question.text: Which of the following is a function of SEBI under the SEBI Act, 1992?

answer.text: Promoting and regulating self-regulatory organisations, prohibiting fraudulent and unfair trade practices in securities markets, and promoting investor education and training of intermediaries
Only prohibiting fraudulent and unfair trade practices relating to securities markets
Only promoting investors' education and training of intermediaries
Only promoting and regulating self-regulatory organisations

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 11 of the SEBI Act lists each of these as a specific function of SEBI: promoting and regulating self-regulatory organisations, prohibiting fraudulent and unfair trade practices in securities markets, and promoting investor education and the training of intermediaries. The Trap: Each narrower option is a real SEBI function, but none of them alone captures the full scope tested here. The keyed option groups all three statutory functions together as a single standalone enumeration. Note: Section 11 of the SEBI Act sets out SEBI's functions to protect investors and regulate the securities market, and the three functions listed here all appear in the same statutory enumeration.
